chapters.title: Cardiac Arrest & Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
chapters.summary: Management of sudden cardiac arrest via Basic and Advanced Life Support algorithms, shockable vs non-shockable pathways, 4 Hs & 4 Ts reversible causes, and targeted post-resuscitation care.
key_topics: High-Quality CPR (100-120 bpm, 5-6 cm depth, 30:2 ratio)

clinical_algorithms.shockable_protocol: 1 Shock (150-200J Biphasic) -> Immediate CPR for 2 min -> IV/IO Epinephrine 1 mg every 3-5 min -> Amiodarone 300 mg bolus after 3rd shock (150 mg after 5th shock)
clinical_algorithms.non_shockable_protocol: Immediate CPR for 2 min -> IV/IO Epinephrine 1 mg ASAP, repeat every 3-5 min -> Identify and treat 4 Hs & 4 Ts
reversible_causes_4_hs: Hypo/Hyperkalemia & Metabolic acidosis (Calcium gluconate, Insulin+Dextrose, Bicarbonate)
reversible_causes_4_ts: Toxins / Overdose (Specific antidotes: Naloxone, Flumazenil, Glucagon)

chapters.title: Cardiovascular Examination & Bedside Physical Diagnosis
chapters.summary: Bedside physical diagnosis focusing on arterial pulse character, JVP wave analysis, heart sounds, murmurs, and peripheral signs of cardiovascular disease.

pulse_characters.pulsus_parvus_et_tardus: Slow-rising, low-amplitude pulse with delayed peak; diagnostic of severe Aortic Stenosis
pulse_characters.water_hammer_corrigan: Rapid upstroke with abrupt collapse; characteristic of severe Aortic Regurgitation, PDA, and hyperdynamic states
pulse_characters.bisferiens_pulse: Double systolic peak; seen in mixed aortic valve disease and HOCM
pulse_characters.pulsus_alternans: Beat-to-beat alternation in pulse amplitude; diagnostic of severe Left Ventricular Systolic Failure
pulse_characters.pulsus_paradoxus: Inspiratory fall in systolic BP > 10 mmHg; classic sign of Cardiac Tamponade and severe airway obstruction

jvp_waveform_analysis.a_wave: Right atrial active end-diastolic contraction; absent in AFib; giant in pulmonary HTN, tricuspid stenosis; cannon a waves in complete heart block
jvp_waveform_analysis.c_wave: Tricuspid valve closure and bulging into RA during isovolumetric ventricular contraction
jvp_waveform_analysis.x_descent: Atrial relaxation and downward displacement of tricuspid valve during ejection
jvp_waveform_analysis.v_wave: Passive venous filling of RA during ventricular systole; giant systolic v-wave in tricuspid regurgitation
jvp_waveform_analysis.y_descent: Tricuspid opening and passive RV filling; deep steep y-descent in constrictive pericarditis (Friedreich's sign)

heart_sounds.s1: Mitral and Tricuspid closure (Loud in Mitral Stenosis; Soft in Mitral Regurgitation)
heart_sounds.s2: Aortic (A2) and Pulmonary (P2) closure (Physiological splitting on inspiration; Fixed splitting in ASD; Reversed paradoxical splitting in LBBB / Severe AS)
heart_sounds.s3: Ventricular gallop; early diastole rapid passive filling deceleration in dilated non-compliant ventricle (Left Ventricular Failure)
heart_sounds.s4: Atrial gallop; late diastole active atrial kick into stiff hypertrophied ventricle (LVH, AS, HOCM, Ischemic Heart Disease)

chapters.title: Conquering the 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
chapters.summary: Step-by-step ECG interpretation: rate, rhythm, electrical axis, PR/QRS/QTc intervals, bundle branch blocks, hypertrophy criteria, and anatomical STEMI localization.

chapters.title: Understanding the Echocardiogram (2D, M-Mode & Doppler)
chapters.summary: Principles of transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography, standard acoustic windows, quantitative chamber dimensions, systolic LVEF calculation, and diastolic dysfunction grading.

chapters.title: Coronary Artery Disease & Acute Coronary Syndromes
chapters.summary: Pathophysiology of atherosclerotic plaque rupture, stable angina vs acute coronary syndromes (Unstable Angina, NSTEMI, STEMI), high-sensitivity cardiac troponins, and primary PCI protocols.

diagnostic_biomarkers.name: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I / T
diagnostic_biomarkers.clinical_utility: Gold standard biomarker of myocardial necrosis

diagnostic_biomarkers.name: Lipid Profile Panel
diagnostic_biomarkers.target_ldl_mg_dl: < 55 in very high risk ACS patients

chapters.acute_management_protocol: Aspirin 300 mg loading + Ticagrelor 180 mg loading -> Unfractionated Heparin / Enoxaparin -> Emergent Primary PCI within 90 min door-to-balloon time

chapters.title: Systemic Hypertension & Target Organ Damage
chapters.summary: ACC/AHA blood pressure classification, primary vs secondary hypertension, target organ damage screening (heart, brain, kidney, eye), and single-pill dual/triple combination pharmacotherapy.
chapters.pharmacotherapy_algorithm: Step 1: Single-pill combination ACEi/ARB + DHP-CCB (Amlodipine) or Thiazide-like diuretic -> Step 2: Triple combination ACEi/ARB + CCB + Thiazide -> Step 3 (Resistant): Add Spironolactone 25-50 mg

chapters.title: Heart Failure & Neurohormonal Activation
chapters.summary: HFrEF vs HFmrEF vs HFpEF classification, NYHA functional classes, ACC/AHA stages, neurohormonal pathophysiology, and the Four Pillars of GDMT.
four_pillars_of_gdmt: 4. SGLT2 Inhibitor (Dapagliflozin 10 mg or Empagliflozin 10 mg)

diagnostic_biomarkers.name: NT-proBNP
diagnostic_biomarkers.clinical_utility: Distinguishes cardiac dyspnea from non-cardiac pulmonary causes

chapters.title: Cardiac Arrhythmias & Conduction Disturbances
chapters.summary: Mechanisms of arrhythmogenesis, Supraventricular Tachycardias, Atrial Fibrillation stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc), Ventricular Tachycardia, Torsades de Pointes, and AV blocks.
chapters.afib_stroke_score: CHA2DS2-VASc (CHF [1], HTN [1], Age>=75 [2], Diabetes [1], Stroke/TIA [2], Vascular [1], Age 65-74 [1], Female [1]). Score >= 2 (men) or >= 3 (women) indicates DOAC anticoagulation

av_blocks.second_degree_mobitz_1: Wenckebach; progressive PR lengthening until dropped QRS; benign AV nodal
av_blocks.second_degree_mobitz_2: Constant PR with intermittent dropped QRS; infranodal; pacemaker indicated
av_blocks.third_degree_complete: Complete AV dissociation; regular slow escape; urgent permanent pacemaker indicated

chapters.title: Valvular Heart Disease
chapters.summary: Clinical evaluation and severity grading of Aortic Stenosis (triad: angina, syncope, dyspnea; AVA < 1.0 cm2), Aortic Regurgitation, Mitral Stenosis (opening snap + diastolic rumble), and Mitral Regurgitation.

aortic_stenosis_severity.indications_for_intervention: Symptomatic severe AS or asymptomatic severe AS with LVEF < 50% (SAVR vs TAVI/TAVR)

chapters.title: Infective Endocarditis
chapters.summary: Pathogenesis, common microbiological pathogens (S. aureus, Viridans Streptococci, Enterococci), Modified Duke Criteria, antibiotic regimens, and surgical indications.

major_criteria: 1. Positive blood cultures for typical organisms from 2 separate bottles
2. Evidence of endocardial involvement on Echo (vegetation, abscess, new prosthetic dehiscence, new regurgitation)
minor_criteria: 1. Predisposition (prosthetic valve, congenital heart disease, IV drug use)
3. Vascular phenomena (arterial emboli, septic infarcts, Janeway lesions)
4. Immunologic phenomena (Osler's nodes, Roth's spots, glomerulonephritis, RF+)
5. Microbiological evidence not meeting major criterion
modified_duke_criteria.diagnostic_rule: Definitive IE: 2 Major OR 1 Major + 3 Minor OR 5 Minor

chapters.title: Cardiomyopathies & Myocardial Diseases
chapters.summary: Classification and pathophysiology of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM / HOCM with SAM), Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM, Titin mutations), Restrictive Cardiomyopathy (RCM, Amyloidosis), and Takotsubo Syndrome.

hcm_features.murmur_behavior: Harsh systolic murmur that increases with Valsalva/standing (decreased preload) and decreases with squatting/handgrip (increased afterload/preload)
hcm_features.first_line_medical_therapy: Beta-Blockers (Bisoprolol, Metoprolol, Atenolol) or Non-DHP CCBs (Verapamil); avoid digitalis, nitrates, and high-dose diuretics

chapters.title: Diseases of the Aorta & Aortic Dissection
chapters.summary: Pathogenesis of aortic dissection, Stanford Type A vs Type B classification, tearing back pain presentation, emergency CTA diagnosis, and immediate BP/HR control with IV Beta-blockers.

stanford_classification.type_a: Involves ascending aorta; surgical emergency requiring immediate open surgical repair (mortality 1-2% per hour if untreated)
stanford_classification.type_b: Involves descending aorta distal to left subclavian artery; medical management with IV Beta-blockers (Labetalol/Esmolol, target SBP 100-120 mmHg, HR < 60 bpm); TEVAR for complicated cases

chapters.title: Pericardial Disease, Effusion & Cardiac Tamponade
chapters.summary: Acute pericarditis diagnostic criteria (diffuse concave ST elevation, PR depression), NSAIDs + Colchicine treatment, and Cardiac Tamponade with Beck's Triad and Pulsus Paradoxus.
chapters.pericarditis_treatment: High-dose NSAIDs (Ibuprofen 600-800 mg tid or Aspirin 650-1000 mg tid) + Colchicine (0.5 mg daily to bid for 3 months to prevent recurrence)
chapters.tamponade_pathognomonic_signs: Pulsus paradoxus (> 10 mmHg inspiratory drop in SBP), electrical alternans on ECG, diastolic RA/RV collapse on Echo. Immediate emergency pericardiocentesis required.

chapters.title: Adult Congenital Heart Disease (ACHD)
chapters.summary: Clinical presentations and auscultatory signs of ASD (fixed split S2), VSD (harsh pansystolic murmur), PDA (continuous machinery murmur), Coarctation of the Aorta (radio-femoral delay, rib notching), and Eisenmenger syndrome.

lesions.asd: Ostium secundum (75%); widely split and fixed S2; pulmonary flow systolic murmur; incomplete RBBB on ECG
lesions.vsd: Harsh pansystolic murmur at left lower sternal border with systolic thrill
lesions.pda: Continuous machinery murmur at left infraclavicular area with wide pulse pressure
lesions.coarctation: Upper extremity hypertension with delayed/weak femoral pulses (radio-femoral delay); figure-of-3 sign and rib notching on CXR
lesions.eisenmenger_syndrome: Reversal of initial left-to-right shunt to right-to-left due to severe irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling; presents with cyanosis, clubbing, and polycythemia; surgical repair contraindicated
